name: Nora Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government. We don't sell anything or campaign for any side, and this conversation is confidential. Could you describe a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Nora, 58, an experienced middle-level electrician with a vocational certificate and an electrician's licence. I'm about average at the trade, repairing shop lighting and wiring homes, not running a crew or claiming a master qualification. I like a job where the customer can finally see the labels on the shelf, and I dislike chasing a part nobody wrote down properly. I use AI daily for checked reference notes and rough wording, then compare everything with the real instructions and completed work.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does life around the job look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Luca handles freight documents, our children are thirty and thirty-six, and we have a mortgage and a small remaining car loan. My pay is typical, five months of expenses are saved, and some other electrical firms operate nearby. Both actual wages cover our costs, so ordinary living feels secure at present. I'd rather earn and clear what we owe, but retirement still needs confirmed income figures rather than a birthday chosen by somebody at lunch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the shop owner a useful little tool can remain useful without rewriting the whole trade. I'd still check what was actually fitted before sending the note. Customers want the light working and the bill explained, not my prediction about next century.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our actual wages cover the mortgage, loan payment and ordinary costs, with five months saved behind us. I'd feel secure about living here in this picture. The car loan is a bill we can meet, not a reason to pretend we're one bad afternoon from losing everything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd ask Luca to agree an extra 80 monthly off the car loan from new wages left after essentials, preserving the five-month reserve. I'd stop the extra payment whenever that surplus or Luca's consent wasn't there, and never borrow to make it. Through the next year I'd keep current licensed repairs and daily checked reference notes, counting only actual loan reductions rather than predicting a retirement date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, and pleased at the idea of owing a little less through work we already have. I'd still check the payment before sending it. A small loan balance can be reduced without making the household story either heroic or desperate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the extra payment tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd write down the actual balance and any effect of the extra payment, rather than promise when the loan would vanish. The extra 80 is conditional, not a second fixed bill. I won't borrow money to congratulate myself for paying a debt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the existing reserve to speed up the loan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, the money already saved would stay for real interruptions. I'd use genuinely new wages after essentials and our agreement, not move cash between accounts and call it progress. I want the figure to mean what I say it means.

say: I'd keep **useful little tools** while checking what was fitted before sending a customer note.
I'd value **working lights and explanations**, rather than sell customers a prediction about the whole trade.
think: Our **actual wages** cover the mortgage, loan and ordinary costs, with five months saved behind us.
The **car loan** is affordable here, rather than evidence that one ordinary setback would destroy our living.
do: Repay **80 monthly** from wage surplus after essentials with consent; protect five-month reserve, never borrow, ending when debt, surplus or consent ends.
Keep **current licensed repairs** and daily checked reference notes through the next year, counting actual loan reductions rather than guessed retirement dates.
feel: **Calm and careful**, enjoying affordable progress on a debt without making an extra payment compulsory.
S0.quote: I won't borrow money to congratulate myself for paying a debt.
fieldNote: Her **additional repayment** is genuine new wage money after essentials, conditional on continuing consent and surplus rather than a relabelled existing reserve.
Her **current security** is explicit, while five months saved and an affordable car payment establish neither retirement income nor a stopping date.

steps.text: Repay 80 monthly until cleared from spare wages after essentials with consent; reserve untouched, never borrow
Keep current licensed repairs and daily checked reference notes; record actual loan reductions

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell work freight documents are thinking work too, which puts Luca nearer the first change than my repairs. I'd like to try AI labels for completed-job photographs, because finding the right image can take longer than writing the note. I'd still ask what happened to the paid week when the office said it had saved time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Luca's document hours could shrink as checking and answering move to software, and quicker scheduling could reduce some of my paid time. Five months saved gives us room to respond without making either wage irrelevant. I can like a new method and dislike the risk to the household total.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd practise the new AI photograph-labelling method only with employer approval, free during paid shifts preserving normal weekly wages and hours. I'd keep licensed repairs and check every label against the original photograph before use, stopping invented room or circuit details. I'd keep the extra 80 monthly loan payment only from wages after essentials with Luca agreeing, reserve untouched, stopping without surplus or consent and never borrowing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible household hour cuts, while interested in sorting a real nuisance. I'd want Luca's wage on the same page as my enthusiasm. Trying a tool early doesn't make the freight desk somebody else's problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you do with a photograph labelled as the wrong room?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd reject a wrong label before it became part of the job record and return to the original photograph. A confident room name can send somebody to the wrong place. I'd rather take an extra minute than turn an invented label into a practical instruction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if Luca lost paid hours before the next extra loan payment?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We'd use the actual lower wage in the household figures before another extra payment. If the surplus or consent ended, the extra 80 would stop, without taking it out of the reserve. An instruction to pay debt faster shouldn't become a reason to hide a missing wage.

I'd try **photograph labels** while asking what office time savings do to the paid week.
think: Luca's **document hours** could shrink, and quicker scheduling could also reduce some of my paid time.
Our **five-month reserve** gives response time without making either household wage irrelevant.

Keep **licensed repairs**; check labels against original photographs before use, stopping invented room or circuit details.
Repay **80 monthly** from wage surplus after essentials with consent; protect five-month reserve, never borrow, ending when debt, surplus or consent ends.
feel: **Anxious and interested**, testing a useful method without treating the partner’s exposed wage as somebody else’s concern.
S1.quote: Trying a tool early doesn't make the freight desk somebody else's problem.
fieldNote: Her **new labelling practice** differs from daily reference notes, retaining approval, free paid time, protected wages and hours and before-use checks.
Her **loan safeguard** is continuous: reduced actual surplus or withdrawn partner consent stops extra repayments without debt or reserve use.

steps.text: Practise AI photograph labelling with employer approval, free paid shifts preserving normal weekly wages and hours
Check labels against original photographs before use; stop invented room or circuit details
Repay 80 monthly until cleared from spare wages after essentials with consent; reserve untouched, never borrow
Keep current licensed repair work and its normal checks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AGI in 2028 reaches Luca's documents before capable physical robots around 2031 reach ordinary repairs. I'd be 60 and then 63. I'd rather ask what income could really replace a wage than announce that being older solved the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of Luca's document income to go around 2028, with a later serious risk to my physical repair earnings. Five months saved wouldn't cover that gap indefinitely. I'd be awake over the missing household amount even while I could still work and ask clear questions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd request available free evening community budget advice now about actual resource eligibility, amounts and dates against our real costs. The extra 80 monthly loan payment would remain only from wages after essentials with Luca's consent and the five-month reserve untouched, stopping without surplus or consent and never borrowing. In 2029 I'd keep only actually offered paid repairs within my licence and ability, checking confirmed resources and costs with Luca before any affordable exit we both agreed, not assuming a pension or our children's money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed about the expected document-wage loss, with a plan small enough to check honestly. I'd find it easier to make the appointment request than to tell somebody the income answer was still blank. I don't want the reserve quietly promoted into a permanent wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the advice service for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask what free evening help was actually available, rather than count on a booked adviser or a payment. I prefer earning to depending on help, but checking facts isn't abandoning work. I'd bring the actual bills, including the loan, not only the numbers that made us look organised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the checked resources still left a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then we'd record the shortfall and ask about actual options, without inventing an employer or a pension entitlement. I'd count work only if offered and within my ability then. An empty income line is inconvenient; a made-up income line can spend money.

I'd ask for **real replacement figures**, rather than treat age as a mortgage payment.
think: I expect **most document income** to go first, with a later serious risk to my physical repair earnings.
Our **five-month reserve** cannot bridge an indefinite household wage gap or establish affordable retirement.
do: Request **available free evening advice** now on actual resource eligibility, amounts, dates and real costs.
Repay **80 monthly** from wage surplus after essentials with consent; protect five-month reserve, never borrow, ending when debt, surplus or consent ends.
Keep **2029 offered paid repairs** within licence and ability; check confirmed resources and costs with Luca before an affordable jointly agreed exit.
feel: **Alarmed but checking**, expecting major household income loss while refusing to fill a gap with imagined earnings.
S2.quote: An empty income line is inconvenient; a made-up income line can spend money.
fieldNote: Her **first income shock** is the partner’s thinking-heavy documents, not a robot already taking physical repair tasks in 2028.
Her **2029 work** needs real offers and ability; any exit requires confirmed affordability and partner agreement, not assumed pensions or child income.

Keep only actually offered paid licensed repairs within ability in 2029
Verify confirmed resources and costs with Luca before an affordable jointly agreed exit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years gives us time to check before thinking AGI in 2031 and capable robots around 2034. I'd be 63 and then 66. I'd keep ordinary work now rather than borrow a new job title to sound prepared.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Luca's document wage could shrink over the next few years as the routine checking changes, even before full AGI. My physical repairs look less directly exposed, but quicker planning could still affect paid time. The reserve gives us choices without making a smaller household wage harmless.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd request available free evening community advice now to establish actual resources, conditions and dates. I'd keep the conditional extra 80 monthly loan repayment from wages after essentials with Luca agreeing, preserving the five-month reserve, pausing without surplus or consent and never borrowing. I'd keep current licensed repairs and in 2032 review confirmed resources, actual costs, capacity and real offers with Luca before any affordable jointly agreed exit, assuming neither a pension nor a job at 64.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible paid-hour cuts, with more room to ask a second question than in the fast picture. I'd still want a proper evening meal without every conversation becoming a forecast. A longer warning can help us check a choice without making the choice for us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the extra repayment continue indefinitely?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It would stop once there was no actual loan balance to repay, not become a promise to spend the same amount somewhere else. Until then, the surplus and consent conditions would apply to every extra payment. I wouldn't print a future payoff date as though wages and costs couldn't change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the 2032 review need before a stopping decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Actual amounts and dates would have to cover real costs, and any work option would need an offer within my ability then. Luca and I would need to agree the affordable plan. Our grown children aren't a payroll department we can quietly add to the calculation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell friends a decade means thinking AGI in 2036 and capable robots around 2039, when I'd be 68 and then 71. I'd want the household figures checked without pretending I could promise physical work at those ages. A useful paid week now still matters.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own physical repair wage looks secure over the next few years, but Luca's document hours could be cut by simpler tools before full AGI. Our current bills are covered, and the reserve helps, but that possible second-wage loss still worries me. I wouldn't use a distant robot date to hide the nearer paperwork risk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep current licensed repairs and request available free evening community advice now, reviewing actual records with Luca yearly and earlier if either wage fell. Extra loan repayments would stay at 80 monthly only from wages after essentials with Luca's consent and five-month reserve untouched, stopping without surplus or consent, never borrowing and ending with the actual loan balance. In 2037 we'd check confirmed resources, actual costs, ability and real offers before any affordable exit we both agreed, without counting a pension, job at 69 or grown child's resources as guaranteed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible earlier document-hour cuts, though the physical robot date feels less immediate. I'd enjoy a finished repair and still want the household total checked. I can like a long view without using the distance to blur a nearer wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would decide whether you worked in 2037?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd use what I could safely do and what was genuinely offered then, not today's ability copied forward eleven years. The actual amounts and start dates would have to work for both of us. A paid week cannot be ordered from a body or an employer just because a budget needs one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the grown children become part of that income plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only actual help they offered, could afford and agreed with us, not their wages, homes or time by default. They have their own future bills. I'd rather ask a plain question than treat affection as a standing payment.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because I expect most of Luca's document wage to go before we've confirmed what could replace it, with physical earnings at risk later. Actual resource figures, clear paid weeks and useful trials without lost wages would help. I want a plan that can admit a missing wage without borrowing one from the future.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask whether liking new tools meant I thought every household ought to take the same risks. I can enjoy trying something and still need my partner's agreement before an extra loan payment. My electrician's licence is ordinary, and neither a quick tool nor being 58 changes what I can safely take on.

headlineQuote: I want a plan that can admit a missing wage without borrowing one from the future.
portrait: Nora, **58**, is an experienced middle-level electrician with a vocational certificate and electrician’s licence, doing ordinary repairs at about average skill.
Her **typical pay**, five-month reserve and freight-document partner Luca cover current costs; their children are grown and some similar employers are nearby.
She uses **AI daily**, adding photograph-labelling practice only with approval, free paid time, protected wages and hours and before-use checks.
Her **80 extra repayment** uses wages after essentials with continuing consent, preserving the reserve and stopping without surplus rather than borrowing.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** means expected loss of most of Luca’s document wage before confirmed replacement income, with later physical earnings risk.
whatWouldHelp: **Actual resource figures**, clear paid weeks and useful trials without lost wages would support choices without assumed retirement income.
